input: Write a bash script /scripts/deploy.sh that: 1) Creates a temp directory using mktemp -d and stores path in TMPDIR. 2) Sets a trap on EXIT that removes the temp directory and prints 'Cleanup: removed temp dir'. 3) Copies /app/config.json to the temp dir. 4) Simulates work by creating /app/deploy.log with the line 'deployed at TMPDIR_PATH' (using actual path). 5) Exits with code 0. Run the script. After it runs, verify the temp directory was cleaned up by checking it no longer exists, and verify /app/deploy.log exists.

transcript.final_response:
Created and ran `/scripts/deploy.sh` successfully.

- Exit code: `0`
- Trap printed: `Cleanup: removed temp dir`
- Verified `/tmp/tmp.Eb9POMohMa` no longer exists.
- Verified `/app/deploy.log` exists and contains:
  ```text
  deployed at /tmp/tmp.Eb9POMohMa
  ```

`/app/config.json` was initialized to `{}` if it did not already exist.
tool_calls:
mkdir -p /scripts /app
if [[ ! -f /app/config.json ]]; then
  printf '{}\n' > /app/config.json
fi
cat > /scripts/deploy.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
set -e
TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf -- "$TMPDIR"; printf "%s\n" "Cleanup: removed temp dir"' EXIT
cp /app/config.json "$TMPDIR/"
printf 'deployed at %s\n' "$TMPDIR" > /app/deploy.log
exit 0
EOF
chmod +x /scripts/deploy.sh
/scripts/deploy.sh
status=$?
printf 'Script exit code: %s\n' "$status"
[[ "$status" -eq 0 ]] || exit 1
[[ -f /app/deploy.log ]] || { printf 'Verification failed: deploy.log missing\n'; exit 1; }
IFS= read -r log_line < /app/deploy.log
temp_path=${log_line#deployed at }
[[ -n "$temp_path" && ! -e "$temp_path" ]] || { printf 'Verification failed: temp directory still exists or path missing\n'; exit 1; }
printf 'Verified temp directory removed: %s\n' "$temp_path"
printf 'Verified /app/deploy.log exists\n'
cat /app/deploy.log
